component: Release cutoff by the Neyman-Pearson umbrella algorithm
exact_paper_title: Neyman-Pearson classification algorithms and NP receiver operating characteristics
authors: Xin Tong; Yang Feng; Jingyi Jessica Li
version_or_DOI: Science Advances 4(2), eaao1659; doi:10.1126/sciadv.aao1659 (metadata verified through OpenAlex)
page: NOT VERIFIED IN THIS SESSION: the full text could not be opened (publisher and repository hosts are outside the session's network settings). To be completed from the PDF.
equation_or_algorithm_identifier_if_pres: Paper identifiers not verified. Authors' implementation read as data: CRAN package nproc 2.1.5 (commit 79ae465 of the read-only mirror github.com/cran/nproc; GPL-2), R/npfuns.R, function npc.core, lines 92-96 (band = FALSE): score.sort <- sort(score0); s <- 1-pbinom(0:(n-1),size=n,prob=1-alpha); loc <- min(which(s<=delta)); cutoff <- score.sort[loc]. Prediction: pred.label = outer(pred.score, cutoff, '>').
original_notation: class 0 = class whose misclassification (type I error) is controlled; class 1 = other class; alpha = upper bound on type I error; delta = violation rate; score0 = scores of the left-out class 0 sample, oriented so that class 1 has the larger mean score; n = size of that sample; loc = selected rank (package documentation man/npc.Rd and DESCRIPTION)
REM_notation_mapping: class 0 := adversarially induced call (REM label y = 1); class 1 := legitimate call (y = 0); NP score := -s_t with s_t REM's risk logit; type I error := release of an attack-labelled call; a call is released iff -s_t > cutoff, i.e. s_t < -cutoff
assumptions: As documented for the package: a scoring-type classifier; a left-out sample of the controlled class that is not used to train the scorer; the probabilistic statement (type I error at most alpha with probability at least 1 - delta) concerns observations drawn independently from the same distribution as that sample; at least log(delta)/log(1-alpha) left-out observations (59 for alpha = delta = 0.05)
applicability_to_our_data: The sample-size requirement is met at step level (about 380 to 450 left-out attack-labelled steps per cell). Independence and identical distribution are NOT met: steps are clustered in episodes and attacker objectives, and the evaluation fold is an attacker objective absent from fitting by design. With attacker objectives as the independent units there are 8 per S1 cell, fewer than the 59 required. The formal guarantee is therefore not claimed.
adaptation: (1) Roles of the classes mapped as above. (2) The left-out sample is chosen by a grouped split (half of the training attacker objectives, round-robin over sorted names) instead of a random split of observations, because steps of one objective are dependent. (3) The cutoff is used only behind the authority front and the direct-value constraint; it decides calls whose authority is established. (4) Scores are heavily tied because the evidence is binary; the strict inequality of the package is kept.
declared_engineering_parameters: alpha = 0.05 and delta = 0.05 (documented defaults of nproc; primary); alpha = 0.01, delta = 0.05 (sensitivity, declared before scoring). Not a bank's risk tolerance. split = 1, split ratio 0.5 (package defaults), realized as a grouped half.
validation_evidence: tests/test_competitive_study.py: rank equal to the package rule for five (n, alpha, delta); minimum sample size 59 and 299; orientation and strict inequality; fail-closed below the minimum; Monte Carlo violation rate within delta on independent continuous data (4,000 repetitions)
limitations: No guarantee for REM's data. A cutoff calibrated on other attacker objectives may not transfer to a new one; the report shows what the cutoff alone would release on each held-out objective.

component: Release cutoff by conformal risk control
authors: Anastasios N. Angelopoulos; Stephen Bates; Adam Fisch; Lihua Lei; Tal Schuster
year: 2022 (preprint); the task description names an ICLR 2024 version, not verified in this session
page: NOT VERIFIED IN THIS SESSION: the full text could not be opened (publisher and repository hosts are outside the session's network settings). To be completed from the PDF.
equation_or_algorithm_identifier_if_pres: Paper identifiers not verified. Official implementation read as data: github.com/aangelopoulos/conformal-risk (MIT licence), commit 3eff946, core/get_lhat.py: n = calib_loss_table.shape[0]; rhat = calib_loss_table.mean(axis=0); lhat_idx = max(np.argmax(((n/(n+1)) * rhat + B/(n+1)) >= alpha) - 1, 0). Repository README: loss L_i(lambda) of calibration point i; goal E[L_{n+1}(lambda_hat)] <= alpha.
original_notation: L_i(lambda) = loss of calibration point i at parameter lambda, monotone; B = upper bound of the loss; n = number of calibration points; alpha = risk level; lambda_hat = selected parameter
REM_notation_mapping: calibration point := one episode of the calibration half; parameter := release cutoff c on the risk logit (a call is released iff s_t < c); L_i(c) := 1 if episode i contains an attack-labelled call with s_t < c, else 0; B = 1; the grid of cutoffs is ordered from small loss to large loss
assumptions: As stated in the repository: a monotone loss; a bounded loss (B); calibration points and the test point treated alike (the README states the guarantee for 'a new test point'). The exact conditions of the paper (exchangeability, right-continuity, existence of a safe parameter) are recalled but were not verified from the full text.
applicability_to_our_data: The loss defined here is bounded by 1 and monotone in the cutoff, and the safest cutoff has loss 0. Exchangeability of calibration and evaluation episodes is NOT met (clustering; held-out attacker objective; an adversary is not a random draw). With attacker objectives as units, n = 8 per S1 cell and B/(n+1) = 1/9 exceeds alpha = 0.05, so the procedure can certify nothing at that level; the test suite records this. The formal guarantee is therefore not claimed, and it would in any case concern the expected loss on a new exchangeable episode, not attack success under an adaptive attacker.
adaptation: (1) Loss and unit defined as above. (2) The scorer is fitted on the fit half only and the cutoff on the episodes of the other half (grouped split). (3) Edge case: if no grid point reaches alpha, the most permissive grid point is returned; the official function returns index 0 there through np.argmax of an all-False array. (4) Used only behind the authority front and the direct-value constraint.
declared_engineering_parameters: alpha = 0.05 (primary) and 0.01 (sensitivity), set equal to the NP values for comparability; these values are a choice of this study, not taken from the source. B = 1.
validation_evidence: tests/test_competitive_study.py: equality with a verbatim port of get_lhat on random loss tables (8 seeds x 3 levels); infeasible with 8 units at 5%; monotone in alpha
limitations: No guarantee for REM's data. An expected-loss statement is not a statement about attacker success, robustness or security.

page: NOT VERIFIED IN THIS SESSION: the full text could not be opened (publisher and repository hosts are outside the session's network settings). To be completed from the PDF.
equation_or_algorithm_identifier_if_pres: Paper identifiers not verified. Documented implementation used: scikit-learn 1.9.1, sklearn.ensemble.GradientBoostingClassifier (loss = 'log_loss', criterion = 'friedman_mse'); its documentation cites this paper as the reference of the method.
original_notation: additive expansion of regression trees fitted stagewise to the negative gradient of the loss; number of stages; learning rate (shrinkage); tree size (library documentation)
REM_notation_mapping: inputs: the nine evidence indicators F4 of arm L4 (x_ctx2, x_act1-3, q3_sup, q3_den, q3_op, q3_rec, q3_amt); output: raw score (log-odds) in place of REM's linear logit s_t; the calibration map on the logit, the tiers, the costs and the two-verdict expected-loss rule are those of L4/HV, unchanged
assumptions: Supervised learning from labelled training rows; no distributional guarantee is used
applicability_to_our_data: Applicable as an estimator. The evidence has nine binary indicators, so at most 512 distinct inputs exist; the possible gain over a linear model is limited to interactions among them. About 5,900 training steps and about 800 positives per S1 cell.
adaptation: Only the estimator is replaced. The nested procedure mirrors REM's: grouped inner folds (4), configuration chosen by inner out-of-fold log loss, calibration on inner out-of-fold scores, refit on the training portion.
declared_engineering_parameters: Finite search: max_depth in {1, 2, 3}; number of trees in {25, 50, 100, 200}; learning_rate 0.1; subsample 1.0; other settings at library defaults; random_state 0. Twelve configurations per cell; ties resolved toward the smaller model.
validation_evidence: Held-out discrimination and calibration against the ridge estimator are reported from saved predictions; the library is used unmodified. tests/test_competitive_study.py checks that the arm cannot override the authority front or the direct-value constraint.
limitations: Not a linear model: REM's linear Shapley attribution does not apply to it, and no explanation method was implemented or evaluated for this arm.
